chapter_theme: The Lord is within like oil in a sesame seed, and the chapter attacks every outward route to him: Vedas recited in a crowd, the Lord looked for in a palm leaf, ash smeared on a body that has been born and died in every birth, lamps and smeared floors, and the three stones that are broken, trodden and worshipped. Against these it sets the hall (அம்பலம்) that is A, U, M, the beginningless and the dance, the one letter in which the body and the red flame arose, the mother-father who is none but oneself, and the tongue pressed back along the knowledge channel.
structure_note: Questions to the master and to the jnanis (1364, 1366) open the chapter; rebukes to the confused (1365, 1367 to 1369, 1372, 1374, 1376, 1380, 1382, 1386, 1388) alternate with litanies on the hall (1370, 1377, 1378), a hymn of 'you are' (1379), and coded verses on the letters and the yogic body (1371, 1381, 1383, 1385, 1387).

1364.reading: What is it that stood soft, and what, standing apart, touched? Our noble one, you must tell us truly. The one thing that stood as female, standing apart and touching: when that is told truly, release has mingled within.
1364.nuance: The question is put to a teacher (உத்தமா). பெண்மையாக நின்றது ஒன்று (the one that stood as female) is taken as Shakti, who is apart from the soul yet touches it; விட்டுநின்று தொட்டது could also describe the breath or the mind. Release is said to come with the true telling, not with a practice.

1365.reading: If you restrain it, will the universe be held within the five letters? You who know as truth the body taken up by the inner mystery: because you have not recited the six Vedas so as to hold them, does the carrion dog speak in many different ways?
1365.nuance: The syntax does not resolve. உடக்கு is glossed as the inner secret; சடக்கிலாறு வேதம் may be 'six Vedas' or a corrupt phrase; விடக்கு நாய் (a dog after carrion) is an insult for the sectarian who argues. The first line can be read as a sneer or as a real claim that the cosmos is in the five letters.

1366.reading: How the true chakra became the means, how the cool body took on a form, and how it grew white and ripened in water: true jnanis, you must explain this at length.
1366.nuance: The poet asks rather than tells. வெண்மையாகி நீரலே விளைந்து (grown white in water) is taken by tradition as the seed, bindu, from which the body forms, or as the moon's nectar; the verse leaves it as a question. The address விரிந்துரைக்க வேணுமே repeats 1360.

1367.reading: Like oil in a sesame seed our Lord is everywhere and within you, yet you fools swing to and fro; if you can straighten the crooked tail of a thieving dog, you can see the light that stands as the giver in its truth.
1367.nuance: The dog's tail that cannot be straightened is proverbial for the mind that will not be corrected, so the condition is nearly impossible, or a dare: fix the mind and the light is seen. ஊசலாடும் (swinging like a swing) pictures the wavering between outer routes.

1368.reading: You say 'the Pillar is there' in the books you desire, with the knowledge you wanted; you neither hold him nor forget him. The one Pillar is the root channel, the channel within you; apart from seeing him there, everything else is like the confusion of a dream.
1368.nuance: தாணு (the pillar, a name of Siva) is placed in the மூலநாடி, the root channel of yogic anatomy, so the verse makes book-knowledge of God a dream and locates him in the body's channel. தரிக்கிலீர் மறக்கிலீர் (you neither hold nor forget) catches the half-belief of the learned.

1369.reading: You argue in words and waver in your minds, you mutes, like a nazhi measure that has no quarter-measure inside it; four quarter-measures make one nazhi, within you. You argue in words, but the Lord abides within the mind.
1369.nuance: உழக்கு is a quarter of a நாழி, so the image is of a measure that forgets it is made of its parts: the disputants forget that what they argue over is already measured out within. The exact point of the arithmetic is not certain, and தவக்கிறீர் is an unusual form.

1370.reading: A is the hall; the beginningless is the hall; U is the hall; the truth is the hall; M is the hall; form is the hall; Si is the hall: Sivayam has become clear.
1370.nuance: அம்பலம் is the hall of the dance at Chidambaram, repeated eight times until it means the whole. The letters are A, U, M of Om and Si of Siva, so the hall is the mantra; 1377 and 1378 continue the litany with the dance's terrible and wrathful faces and with gold and eternity.

1371.reading: The chakra flew and ran, with a board upon the chakra; like the oil pressed in the mill, air and fire mingled with light in the upper place, and the aeons were thrown into confusion; when it entered the entrance, how did it go?
1371.nuance: The verse is a cipher and ends in a question. சக்கரம் may be the drawn diagram, a wheel, or a centre of the body; the oil-mill repeats the sesame image of 1367; சிங்குவாயு and உக்கிலே are obscure. The question போனவாறது எங்ஙனே (how did it go?) is asked again of the Lord's 'parting' in 1382.

1372.reading: You who count the breast that grew and rose as maya, examine in truth within yourself the body of the jiva that holds grace; if you listen to the words of the great who have gained shining knowledge, the right thought will enter your stainless heart.
1372.nuance: The first line may rebuke those who dismiss the body (or woman) as illusion, in keeping with the poet's praise of the body as Shakti; or கொங்கை may be a figure for the swelling of pride or desire. அருள்கொள் சீவர் ஆர் உடம்பு is loose: 'the body of the grace-bearing souls'.

1373.reading: Do you know the one knowledge that the four Vedas recite? As the knowledge-awakening uttered through the four watches of the night, the poison-throated one, Ayan and Mal, thought on deeply, settled in the heart as Sivayam.
1373.nuance: The one knowledge of the Vedas is Sivayam dwelling in the heart; the three gods are named as its forms, not its rivals. நாலு சாமம் (four watches) matches the four Vedas and may hint at recitation through the night.

1374.reading: What you call 'around' you do not place at the end of scripture; where did it sit, dancing day and night? For devotees ripe in love, the one in the Supreme is a void. Madmen, how can you think this out and speak of it?
1374.nuance: சுற்றும் (around, surrounding) and அத்தம் நித்தம் are unclear; the first line may say that the sectarians never reach the Vedanta where the circling ends. பாழ் (void) is the Siddhars' word for what remains when the Supreme is reached, and the verse denies that it can be reasoned about.

1375.reading: However he stands to be made clear, however they say the Lord graciously rose to his friends, so does the primal supreme self dwell in grace; and the three impurities are cut off like an elephant that a lion has come upon.
1375.nuance: The first two lines are loose, with எங்ஙனே (however) three times picking up the last word of 1371. The plain claim is in the last line: the three malas (anava, karma, maya in Siddhanta) are destroyed by the approach of the Supreme, as a lion kills an elephant.

1376.reading: Within the house, sweeping and smearing the floor, setting out many lamps and performing a puja that deceives; doing good tapas, seeking the feet of the one Lord: the right conduct that is learned, find it within yourselves.
1376.nuance: அற்றவுள் அகம் is unclear: the inner house of the one who has let go, or simply the house. ப்ரவாதபூசை ஏய்த்தியே is obscure, perhaps a puja of mere talk (பிரவாதம்) that cheats. சரிதை is சரியை, the path of outer service; the verse moves it inward.

1377.reading: What stood watching is the hall, the hall where the Supreme dances; what stood as dance is the hall, the terrible is the hall; the word is the hall, fire is the hall, wrath is the hall: Sivayam has become clear.
1377.nuance: The litany of 1370 continues, now with the dance's fierce aspects: கோரம் (the terrible), வன்னி (fire), சீற்றம் (wrath). The hall is not only Chidambaram but every act and mood of the Lord.

1378.reading: Going on from place to place, the fine golden hall; the beginningless hall that stood then and stands now; the hall that is the end and endures for ever; standing joined and joined within, Sivayam was hidden there.
1378.nuance: The hall is found in every place walked to, and is beginningless and final at once. ஒனிந்ததே in the last line is not a word; ஒளிந்ததே (was hidden) or ஒடுங்கியதே (subsided) fit the metre and sense.

1379.reading: You are the father, you are dharma, you are every deity; you are the flood and you are clarity, you yourself are siddhi and mukti; you are bindu and you are the yield, you are the Veda above it all; you are my father, you are the Lord, the Isan who took me as his own.
1379.nuance: A hymn of நீ (you) in a chapter of rebukes. சிந்து may be the sea or river, or a drop; விந்து and விளைவு (bindu and its yield) make the Lord both seed and harvest. என்னை ஆண்ட (who ruled me) is the language of the Nayanmars.

1380.reading: Poor ones, born and dead and perished in every birth, and born again in this one: what is this ash you smear? If, along with the water, you can cut off the impurity and remove desire, you can see clearly in the bell-sound of nada.
1380.nuance: அப்பு is glossed as water, so the ash and the bath are taken together as the outward cleansings, and the verse asks for the cutting of malam and desire instead; another reading makes அப்புடன் மலம் the body's own water and filth. செப்பு நாத ஓசை (the sound of a copper bell, or 'the nada sound I speak of') is the inner sound.

1381.reading: The eightfold yoga and the moving nada, and within the eight letters the U and the A, blossoming apart, the mantra went up through the staff of the veena and settled in the eight letters as Sivayam.
1381.nuance: வீணாதண்டு (the veena's staff) is the spine in yogic reading, so the mantra rises through it. எட்டு அக்கரம் (the eight letters) is not explained; it may be ஓம் நம சிவாய counted as eight, or the eight syllables of a longer formula. The eight of yoga and the eight letters are set side by side without a key.

1382.reading: You fools who babble 'Lord, Lord': how did our Lord ever part from the Lord? As Lord and as Lord and as the great world itself, your body, you madmen, is what sprouted from the Lord.
1382.nuance: The repeated பிரான் makes the point by sound: there is no second Lord to call to, and no distance to cross. The body is not what hides him but what grew out of him, which is the chapter's answer to ash, Vedas and stones.

1383.reading: No beginning, no end, no four Vedas that came to be; no light, no word, a pure space beyond speech; no justice, no love, nothing that can be fixed; once the First is seen, even the five letters are not.
1383.nuance: அஞ்செழித்தும் is a corruption of அஞ்செழுத்தும். The verse strips away even what the chapter elsewhere uses, the five letters, light and the Vedas, and leaves தூவெளி, the pure expanse, which in Tirumular too is the final state. 1340 located the mantra in the mind; here even that is left behind.

1384.reading: Mother-Father: when the Father sat as you, you did not know it; you who became Mother-Father are the bond of the First. Since there is no one but you as Mother-Father, there is no one, no one at all, but you.
1384.nuance: அம்மையப்பன் (Mother-Father) is the one Lord as both, and the verse says the hearer is that one. ஆதியான் பாசமே in line 2 is unclear: 'you are the First's bond', or 'that is the First's bond, that you do not know it'. The doubled இல்லை of the last line is the poet's emphasis.

1385.reading: In the first one letter the red flame sprouted; in that one letter the body was born and formed; in that one letter it stood as one; know and realise that one letter too.
1385.nuance: ஓர் எழுத்து (one letter) is traditionally Om, or the single letter of Siva; the verse does not name it. Flame, body and unity all come from it, and the last line asks for the letter to be known, not recited.

1386.reading: Gathering in a crowd you recite the Veda together; in which letter does the Lord sit inside the palm leaf? Set your gaze and seek within the four and the three; the Mother dances inside the dancing-place: that is the truth, by her oath.
1386.nuance: ஏட்டகத்துள் ஈசன் (the Lord inside the palm leaf) is the chapter's sharpest line against book-learning. நாலுமூன்று (four and three) is coded: seven, as the centres or the worlds, or twelve as their product. ஆட்டகம் is glossed as the place of the dance of bliss, and அம்மை ஆணை is either 'by the Mother's oath' or 'the Mother's rule'.

1387.reading: For the reason the ancients set out, press the tongue, bend it inward and go up through the channel of knowledge; if, watching with longing, you praise the two letters of the mantra, every direction you look becomes the supreme Brahman.
1387.nuance: The tongue bent back and up is the khechari seal of the yoga texts. The first line (காக்கை மூக்கை ஆமையார்) is corrupt: 1180 opens the same formula with ஆக்கை மூப்பது இல்லையே, 'the body does not age', which gives the verse its point. இரண்டெழுத்து (two letters) is read as சிவ or as அ and உ.

1388.reading: You break a ringing stone in two; the stone set in the doorway you tread on until it is worn smooth; on the stone kept for puja you offer flowers and water. Tell me, which stone is the one the Lord is pleased with?
1388.nuance: Three stones from the same quarry: one broken, one a doorstep, one a god. The question has no answer the worshipper can give, which is the point; 1458 asks the same of the planted stone that is circled with flowers and mutterings while the Lord is within.

links.note: Both verses have the Lord as oil in the sesame seed; 1259 adds that he came gently into the poet after true tapas, while 1367 turns the image into a rebuke of fools who swing between outer routes and dares them to straighten the dog's tail.

Tirumular's Lord is ghee in milk, juice in fruit and fragrance in the flower, mingled everywhere; Sivavakkiyar's is oil in the sesame seed. Tirumular leaves the image as praise; Sivavakkiyar uses it to ask why anyone looks elsewhere.

Tirumular says that wearing the holy ash gladly without fail makes deeds fall away and brings the Siva state; Sivavakkiyar asks what use the ash is to one born and dead in every birth, and makes the cutting of malam and desire the condition of seeing. The conflict holds if 1380 denies that the ash does anything; it eases if the poet only ranks it below inner cleansing.

Both verses set ash-smearing beside Vedic recitation and babbling as things that do not bring the Lord: 1001 says he does not come for them, only for a melted heart that speaks the truth within; 1380 says cut malam and desire instead and see in the sound of nada.

The Kural says a spotless mind is the whole of virtue and all else is noisy show; Sivavakkiyar asks what the ash on the body is for and puts the cutting of impurity and desire in its place. Both put inner cleanness over the visible sign.

Tirumular asks what use it is to write the cause beyond all signs on the outside of a palm leaf, without the guru's joining; Sivavakkiyar asks in which letter the Lord sits inside the palm leaf while the crowd recites. Both say the book cannot hold what it names.

Tirumular says that once samadhi is in hand sounded chant, purification and even the mind become needless; Sivavakkiyar says that once the First is seen there is no light, no word and not even the five letters. Both set a stage past the means they otherwise teach.

Tirumular says the world knows letters on water and no one knows the one letter in the sky, and that even its knowers miss the letter in the flesh; Sivavakkiyar says the flame and the body were born in the one letter and asks that it be known. Both put the one letter in the body.

1180 gives the formula whole: the body does not age if the tongue and nose are folded in, the breath passes along the nada channel and the two are pressed tight, and every direction becomes Brahman. 1387 repeats the second half with a corrupt first line and adds the praise of the two-letter mantra; it reads as a variant of 1180.

Tirumular says that if the two breaths are set in the upper palate Death is gone, the door opens and grey hair turns to childhood; Sivavakkiyar presses the tongue back along the knowledge channel and finds Brahman in every direction, and the sister verse 1180 promises that the body does not age.

Kakapusundar warns that those who merely raise the tongue to the palate and stare gain nothing, their eyes burst and the body goes, and that the mind must be set at the palate for the breath to be mastered; Sivavakkiyar's verse gives the tongue practice with the praise of the mantra as its condition. The two agree on the method but Kakapusundar limits it.

Both mock the worshipped stone: 1458 asks whether the planted stone will speak while the Lord is within, as a burnt pot knows no taste of curry; 1388 lines up the broken stone, the doorstep and the puja stone and asks which one pleases the Lord.

Tirumular says that for one who seeks to be saved pearl, ash, rice, flowers or sand can all be made the linga, the Father's body; Sivavakkiyar asks which of three identical stones the Lord could be pleased with. The conflict holds if 1388 rejects image worship outright; it eases if Tirumular's point, that the material is indifferent, is taken as Sivavakkiyar's too.

source_issues: 1378 line 4: ஒனிந்ததே is not a word; ஒளிந்ததே or ஒடுங்கியதே is likely.
1387 line 1 (காக்கை மூக்கை ஆமையார் எடுத்துரைத்த காரணம்) is corrupt; 1180 (sivavakkiyam:216) has the same verse with the first line ஆக்கைமூப்பது இல்லையே, and the two are a doubled unit.
The gloss attached to 1382 (அந்த - முடிவு) belongs to 1383, where அந்தமில்லை occurs; 1382 has no அந்த.
1365 (சடக்கிலாறு வேதமும்) and 1376 (ப்ரவாதபூசை ஏய்த்தியே) have obscure phrases that may be corrupt.
